property_summary: After any call to transferOwnership, the owner must equal the passed _newOwner; the mutant assigns owner to itself, leaving it unchanged, so the check c.owner() == _newOwner fails for any _newOwner different from the current owner.

After a successful call to transferOwnership by the current owner with any new owner address, the owner must equal that _newOwner; the mutant assigns owner to itself, so owner remains unchanged, violating equality for any _newOwner different from the current owner.
After a successful call to transferOwnership by the current owner, the owner must change to the argument supplied; the bug assigns owner to itself, so it never changes.

After any call to transferOwnership, the owner storage variable should equal the argument passed; the buggy version always sets it to address(0), violating this invariant when the argument is non-zero.

After a successful transferOwnership call, the owner must equal the argument if the argument is not the zero address; the buggy version always sets owner to zero, breaking the rule for any non-zero new owner.

After a transferOwnership call, if the caller is the current owner, the owner should equal the passed _newOwner argument; the buggy version always sets owner to address(0), violating this whenever _newOwner != address(0).

After a successful transferOwnership call, the owner must equal the passed _newOwner argument if the current owner is the caller; the buggy version always sets owner to address(0), violating this for any non-zero new owner.
After any successful transferOwnership call, owner must equal the transferred address; the mutant leaves owner unchanged so the assertion fails when the new owner differs from the current one.

After transferOwnership is called by the current owner with a new owner address, the new owner must be able to call a function restricted by the onlyOwner modifier; the bug fails this because owner is never updated, so the original owner still holds the privilege.
After a successful call to transferOwnership by the current owner, the owner state variable must equal the _newOwner argument; the bug leaves owner unchanged.

For any call to transferOwnership from the current owner, the owner must change to the argument address; the mutant leaves owner unchanged, so the new owner cannot be the argument after a successful call.
For any call to transferOwnership from the owner with any non-zero address, the previous owner must cease to have onlyOwner privileges; the mutant leaves the original owner with full control.
After any call to transferOwnership, the old owner must match the caller; the bug violates this by allowing a non-owner to change owner.

For any initial owner and any new owner, after a call to transferOwnership by the current owner, the owner is updated; for any caller who is not the current owner, the call must revert. The bug breaks this by allowing non-owners to change owner without revert.
After any call to transferOwnership by an arbitrary caller, the owner must remain unchanged if the caller is not the original owner; the bug allows non-owners to change the owner.
After any call to transferOwnership, the owner should remain unchanged because the onlyOwner modifier always reverts with require(false), so ownership transfer must never succeed.

For any caller that is not the current owner, a call to transferOwnership(newOwner) must not change the owner; the buggy 'require(false)' modifier makes it revert even for the legitimate owner, so when the owner calls transferOwnership with a new address, the owner does change in the reference but remains stuck in the buggy version.
A successful call to transferOwnership(newOwner) must set owner to newOwner; the buggy require(false) modifier makes every call revert, so owner never updates.
Only the current owner can change the owner, so after any call to transferOwnership that is not from the owner, the owner state variable must remain unchanged.
After any call to transferOwnership, the caller becomes the new owner exactly when the caller was the previous owner; the buggy version lets a non-owner caller become owner.

After any call to transferOwnership, the new owner must equal either the previous owner (if the call reverted) or the argument _newOwner (if the call succeeded); the bug allows a non-owner caller to set owner to any _newOwner.

After any call to transferOwnership, the owner must equal the transferred address; the bug ignores the argument and sets owner to msg.sender instead, so the rule fails when the caller differs from the new owner argument.
After transferOwnership, the owner must equal the transferred address regardless of caller; the bug sets owner to msg.sender instead, violating this when caller differs from the argument.
